title: Sketch what you can’t describe
principle: If you have a layout in your head and no words for it, draw it on paper and upload a photo. Visual intent that resists language still transfers when Claude can see the sketch.
procedure: When words fail, sketch the layout on paper (rough is fine).
Photograph or scan the sketch and upload it.
Ask Claude to interpret the sketch as structure—not to “pretty it up” into a different layout.
Iterate with pointed follow-ups once the structure matches.
examplePrompts: I uploaded a photo of a paper sketch. Recreate this layout structure in HTML—same regions, hierarchy, and proportions. Do not invent a different composition. Ask before changing the structure.
tips: Use this when you can picture the layout but can’t name it.
The sketch is the brief; the prompt should protect that structure.
Pairs well with wireframe-first when fidelity still doesn’t matter.
